title: mudev recipe
description: A Moodle site definition: core (+ optional patches) and a selection of plugins. The same schema validates a source recipe (mdl-recipes/<vendor>/<name>.yaml) and the resolved live recipe written to a checkout's .mudev.json — the latter fully flattened: every plugin's catalogue definition (relpath, source, requirements, ...) merged inline with the checked-out ref (a branch for a dev workspace, or a tag/commit for a pinned edition), so it needs no plugins directory or catalog.

description.description: One-line human summary of what this recipe builds and who it is for.

catalog.description: Where bare-name plugin references resolve. Path relative to this file, or absolute. Defaults to MUDEV_PLUGINS_DIRECTORY when omitted.

contributed_by.description: Credit party for this recipe (also asserts recipe authorship/ownership). The catalogues are CC0: keeping the credit on reuse is a courtesy, not a condition (see the catalogue README). A name or list of names. In a resolved .mudev.json this identifies the project owner, NOT the source recipe author (see based_on_recipe).

based_on_recipe.description: For a live recipe (.mudev.json): the source it was cloned from — a catalogue identifier (vendor/stream/version) or, when cloned from a recipe file, that file's path (provenance). This also credits a catalogue source (courtesy credit, indicating adaptation) — used instead of copying the source's top-level contributed_by. Inlined plugin entries still retain their own contributed_by.

extra.description: Tool-namespaced extension config (composer-style). Each key is a tool name; its value is that tool's own config, opaque to this schema — so tools extend recipes without schema churn. Present at the recipe top level and on each plugin entry. mudev reads two keys. `extra.mudev.release`: a flavour name (string). Recipe-level `release: <flavour>` marks a release workspace under that flavour's rules (tag + version.php $version/$release + changelog); plugin-level `release: <flavour>` marks the plugin release-managed. Absent = read-only build/consume. `extra.mudev.fetch_order`: a list of remote names contacted first, in that order, e.g. [backup, origin] — mudev fetches EVERY remote of every checkout, and this decides who is asked first, so a mirror on the local network fills the object store and leaves the slow remote only the difference to send. Remotes not listed are still fetched, after the listed ones; names a given checkout lacks are skipped. Future consumers (composer assembler, catalogue site) use their own `extra.<tool>` namespace.

mudev.description: mudev's own namespace, and the only one this schema defines. It is CLOSED: every key mudev reads is listed here, so a typo (fetchorder, releases) is a schema error rather than a setting that silently does nothing. mudev's schema and binary ship together, so new keys arrive with the version that reads them. Other tools keep their own extra.<tool> namespace, which this schema does not constrain.

release.description: Release flavour name, e.g. mutms. Recipe-level: this workspace is a release workspace under that flavour's rules (tag + version.php + changelog). Plugin-level: this plugin is release-managed, and the flavour must match the recipe's.

fetch_order.description: Remote names to fetch first, in this order, e.g. [forge, origin]. Must be a LIST, not a comma-separated string. mudev fetches every remote of every checkout; this only decides who is asked first, so a mirror on the local network fills the object store and leaves the slow remote only the difference to send. Unlisted remotes are still fetched afterwards; names a given checkout does not have are skipped.

base.description: The base code tree plugins are installed into: Moodle, or a patched derivative of it.

mdlbranch.description: Moodle $branch code as a string (e.g. "502"). Indexes a plugin's `requirements` block (via its `mdlbranches`) for branch resolution.

source.description: How mudev acquires Moodle core. Normally one `git` kind: `git.remotes.origin` is the clone remote and `git.ref` is the branch (`origin/patch/mutms/MOODLE_502_STABLE`) or a pinned tag.

localbranch.description: Local branch name to create from a branch `source.git.ref` (git `switch -c <localbranch> <ref>`). Defaults to the remote branch name. Use it to drop a prefix — e.g. ref `origin/patch/mutms/MOODLE_502_STABLE` → local `MOODLE_502_STABLE`. Ignored when the ref is a tag/commit.

strippublic.description: Strip the leading public/ from every plugin path (older Moodle branches without the public/ layout).

patches.description: Patch branches merged over ref, in order.

plugins.description: Plugin entries: a bare identifier (resolved via catalog), or an object with per-plugin annotations and/or a full inline definition.

oneOf.description: Bare plugin identifier reference, resolved via catalog.

Reference with overrides, or a full inline plugin definition. Its own fields match the plugin data model (source, relpath, …); the version to check out is `source.git.ref`; tool flags live under `extra`. Left open (additionalProperties) so a reference may carry a partial `source` — e.g. just `source.git.ref` to pin an edition, with remotes merged from the catalogue.

localbranch.description: Local branch name to create from a branch `source.git.ref` (git `switch -c <localbranch> <ref>`). Defaults to the remote branch name. Ignored when the ref is a tag/commit.

extra.description: Tool-namespaced flags for this plugin in this recipe (composer-style; opaque to this schema). mudev reads `extra.mudev.release` — a flavour name (e.g. {release: mutms}) marking the plugin release-managed. Owner state: hand-authored in a source recipe; in the mudev-managed .mudev.json it is set via mudev commands, not by hand.

mudev.description: mudev's own namespace, and the only one this schema defines. It is CLOSED: every key mudev reads is listed here, so a typo (fetchorder, releases) is a schema error rather than a setting that silently does nothing. mudev's schema and binary ship together, so new keys arrive with the version that reads them. Other tools keep their own extra.<tool> namespace, which this schema does not constrain.

release.description: Release flavour name, e.g. mutms. Recipe-level: this workspace is a release workspace under that flavour's rules (tag + version.php + changelog). Plugin-level: this plugin is release-managed, and the flavour must match the recipe's.

fetch_order.description: Remote names to fetch first, in this order, e.g. [forge, origin]. Must be a LIST, not a comma-separated string. mudev fetches every remote of every checkout; this only decides who is asked first, so a mirror on the local network fills the object store and leaves the slow remote only the difference to send. Unlisted remotes are still fetched afterwards; names a given checkout does not have are skipped.

source.description: Acquisition methods for the code, as a map of one-or-more source kinds that can COEXIST — each consumer picks the kind it supports (mudev reads `git`; a composer-based assembler reads `composer`; a plain installer would read `zip`). The kind is the KEY (no `type` discriminator), so a catalogue entry can advertise several ways to get the same plugin at once. Each kind is self-contained — it names where the bits are AND which version: git → `remotes` + `ref`; `composer` → package name (constraint derived from the recipe's release version); a future `zip` → `url` + `sha256`. `git` and `composer` are defined today; `zip` is a reserved sibling.

composer.description: Composer acquisition: the Packagist package name. Presence = published on Packagist; absence = not. The version constraint is derived from the recipe's release version, not stored here.

git.description: Git acquisition: named remotes plus the ref to check out.

remotes.description: Git remotes as name → URL string. `origin` is the primary clone remote; `upstream` (forks) and `backup` (mirror) are optional. A `<remote>/<branch>` ref resolves its remote name here.

ref.description: What to check out. For a branch, git's remote-tracking spelling `<remote>/<branch>` where `<remote>` is a key from `remotes` (default `origin`, e.g. `origin/MOODLE_500_STABLE`); or a tag/commit for a pinned edition. Absent in the public catalogue (resolved per recipe). A recipe reference may set just this (remotes merged from the catalogue).
